title: SpecDiff
description: A proposed amendment to the spec graph: node creations, revisions and retirements plus edge changes. See ADR-0016 and ADR-0017. This is both the ADR-0021 `spec_diff` render payload and the contract a language model's proposal must satisfy before the factory will persist it — an amendment that does not validate here never reaches df.specs.propose.

creates.description: New spec nodes. The factory assigns each a spec_id; a model never invents one.

revises.description: New revisions of existing nodes. The full replacement text, never a patch.

edge_adds.description: Edges point at node identities, not revisions. `new:N` refers to the Nth entry of `creates` (zero-based), which is how a diff can wire up nodes whose ids do not exist yet.

spec_id.description: A ULID in Crockford base32. A model may only reference ids it was actually shown in the context pack; inventing one produces a diff the factory cannot apply.

oneOf.description: A forward reference to `creates[N]` within this same diff.

kind.description: What sort of thing this node is. Deliberately a closed set: an open one becomes a synonym soup within a month of a model choosing freely.

layer.description: Which architectural layer the node belongs to. Open, because layers are a property of the customer's stack and are declared by their standards servers (ADR-0023).

text.description: The specification itself, as a single self-contained statement. ADR-0016's small grain: one behaviour, rule or constraint per node.

rationale.description: Why this change. Rendered in the approval card; not part of the node's canonical content, so it never affects the content hash.

edge_kind.description: ADR-0016's typed edges. Plugin-declared kinds are added to this enum through the convention process, not by a model choosing a new string.
